title: Find All Possible Recipes
hints: a recipe becomes makeable only once every single one of its ingredients is available - and an ingredient becoming available can unlock more recipes, cascading forward
this cascade is exactly Kahn's algorithm: build an in-degree count for every recipe (how many ingredients it still needs), and start the queue with all supply items already marked available
when you pop an available item, look at everything it's an ingredient for, and decrement that recipe's remaining-ingredient count; if it hits zero, the recipe just became available too - enqueue it
once the queue is empty, you have the full set of items that ever became available; intersect that with recipesToCheck and sort the result ascending
commonMistakes: not accounting for recipe cycles, which silently loop forever or incorrectly mark cyclic recipes as makeable
forgetting that a recipe can itself be an ingredient for another recipe (multi-level dependency), and only checking one level of ingredients
not sorting the final result, or including recipe indices that were never actually satisfied

content.problemStatement:
There are `n` items, labeled 0 to n - 1, where recipes and base supplies
share this same numbering. You're given a list of edges, where each edge
`[ingredient, recipe]` means `ingredient` is required to make `recipe`,
plus `supplies`, a list of item indices already available as raw
ingredients, and `recipesToCheck`, a list of item indices to test.

**Return every index from `recipesToCheck` that can actually be made, in ascending order.**

An item can be made if every one of its required ingredients is available, where an ingredient counts as available if it's in `supplies`, or if it is itself a recipe that can be made, using the same rule recursively.
constraints: each edge [ingredient, recipe] has 0 <= ingredient, recipe < n
supplies and recipesToCheck contain valid item indices in range [0, n)
notes: two recipes that require each other, forming a cycle - neither can ever be made
a recipe needing an ingredient that is never supplied and never itself makeable
no edges at all - nothing beyond the initial supplies is makeable
a recipe that requires several other recipes chained several levels deep

item 1 needs both 0 and 2, but 2 is never available; item 3 has no connection to any supply at all

optimal.pattern: Kahn's algorithm: seed the queue with all supplies, and cascade availability forward through the ingredient-to-recipe edges

bruteForce.approach: for each recipe in recipesToCheck, recursively try to make it by resolving each of its ingredients, tracking a 'currently being resolved' set to avoid infinite loops, redoing this work independently for every query
